narrative:
The model estimated a 55% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it judged you slightly more likely to default than to repay. Because this is above the bank’s risk cutoff, your application was denied.

The most important factor was your checking account situation. You have a negative checking account balance. Among approved applicants, negative balances are uncommon; most either have no checking account or a positive balance. This strongly pushed the decision toward bad credit.

The second most important factor was the amount you requested. At 4,006 DM, it is above the approved average of about 3,020 DM, but in your case it actually counted in your favor, pulling the prediction toward good credit. It was not enough to offset the other concerns.

The third factor was that the loan is for a new car. New-car requests are less common among approved applicants than radio/TV or furniture loans, and this added to the bad-credit side.

To improve your chances, bring your checking account into positive territory and keep it there for several months before reapplying. Reassess whether the new-car purchase can wait or be financed differently. Ask the bank what balance and loan purpose they would view as acceptable. Since your requested amount already helped your case, focus first on your account balance and the loan purpose.
